turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Shame, sorry, I'm a bit all over the place, the nights have been so long I hardly know where to start.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's alright, there's no rush. What's been bothering you the most?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): It's my legs. At night they get this creeping feeling, like something crawling under the skin, and I cannot sleep properly.

[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): It starts the moment I lie down, mostly the right leg from the knee to the ankle, and if I move it or walk to the kitchen it eases for a minute, then it comes straight back when I get into bed.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sounds exhausting. How long has the creeping been going on?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): Ja, about three weeks. I counted back to when I turned 27 weeks, I'm 30 weeks now, so three weeks, and it's every single night, not just some of them.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the sleep, tell me what the nights actually look like for you.
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): I do drop off eventually, maybe around midnight, but I wake four or five times because the leg starts again, so the sleep is broken, I'm not awake the whole night.
[SEG0009] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): She was telling me outside she sleeps badly, hardly at all, and that she doesn't take her tablets on Sundays.

[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): No, I wouldn't say hardly at all, I do sleep, it's just broken like I said. And it's not Sundays, it's Saturdays I skip the iron, the red ones, every Saturday, because we go to my mother's and I forget that bottle. The folick acid stays in my bag so I still take that one.
[SEG0011] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Ok, Saturdays. She also showed me a little cut on the shin, said it healed in five days.
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): Ja, that was from the bakkie door, caught the shin, and it closed up in five days, nice and dry, I only mentioned it because I notice every little thing now.
[SEG0013] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): And she said her ankles are quite swollen by the evening.
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): Hey, no, they're not swollen. I said they feel heavy, tired heavy, but there's no puffiness, my shoes fit the same and there aren't even sock marks.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. That cut, any trouble with wounds healing slowly, or did it sort itself out?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No slow healing at all. It was done in five days, clean, no oozing, nothing that hung around.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. What medicines are you taking at the moment?

[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): Every morning by mouth I take the folick acid, five milligrams, I don't miss that one. And the red blood tablets, ferris sulphaite, two hundred milligrams, also by mouth in the morning, except Saturdays.

[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): The red ones are for the low blood, the iron stores, and the folick acid is just the pregnancy tablet, not for the legs. I swallow them with water. My aunt said tea blocks the iron but I only heard that last week, so I've been careful since.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's worth keeping up. Do you know what the ferritin came back as?

[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): The midwife said it was low, eleven or maybe twelve, I scribbled it on a till slip and lost it, so don't quote me. My pressure last time I do remember, it was one thirty over eighty four, because she made me sit and repeat it.
[SEG0022] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I've got today's check here. Blood pressure is 118 over 74, pulse is 88. And the ferritin on the file from last week is 14.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fourteen is on the low side at this stage, which fits. Any headache, or flashing lights, or pain up under the ribs?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): No headache, no flashing lights, no pain under the ribs. I get a bit of heartburn if I eat late, but that's separate, tomato bredie does it every time.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your breathing, your chest, any trouble there at all?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Chest is fine, breathing is normal, I can walk and talk without gasping.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any burning when you pass water, or contractions, or bleeding?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): No burning, no contractions, no bleeding. Baby is wriggling nicely, especially after cold water, more on the left, which is odd because the leg thing is the right.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me about the family, anyone with sugar or pressure or anything like that?

[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties, on tablets, my mother did not, she never had sugar or pressure, she passed in a car accident, not a stroke, I always mix that up. My older sister has pressure but no sugar, and my dad's sister in Pietermaritzburg has thyroid trouble, she's on treatment for it.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): And day to day, what does life look like for you right now?

[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): I work as a bookkeeper at a small firm in Durban, umm about eight hours a day, sometimes I stay till six if month-end is hectic. I eat pretty ordinary, pap and veg and chicken most nights, not much fried stuff. I walk to the taxi rank most mornings, that's my exercise, twenty minutes each way. I don't drink, not since I fell pregnant, I used to have a glass of wine on a Friday, and I never smoked, not even at varsity.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's a long day. Can I have a look at the legs while we talk?
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): Ja, of course. The right one is the bad one at night. The left only joins in if I've stood at the sink too long, but the creeping in bed is the right.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Calves are soft, no redness, no swelling that I can see, and the ankles aren't puffy today.

[SEG0036] person_1 (PATIENT): See, that's what I mean, they look normal in the day. It's once the house is quiet and I'm trying to sleep that the creeping starts, not itchy, more like ants under the skin.

[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): I hear you. With the night-time creeping, the ferritin at 14, and you being 30 weeks, my feeling is restless legs, very common in pregnancy when the iron stores are down. That's a working impression, not something we've proved.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): Ja, restless legs, I read about it on my phone at two in the morning, went down a whole rabbit hole about bananas and baths, sorry, I do that when I can't sleep.

[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): A warm bath is fine if it soothes you. Keep the folick acid and the red blood tablets every morning as you are, and try not to skip the Saturday iron, maybe leave a strip in your handbag.
[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): Ja, I'll put some in the handbag tonight. They don't upset my stomach, so it's not that, it's just me being scatty on a Saturday.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lovely. Let's see you in two weeks, you've already got the midwife check booked then, and we might do a scan of the leg if it does not settle.
[SEG0042] person_3 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Ja, it's in the book, antenatal clinic, two weeks from today, the Tuesday morning with the midwife.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the creeping gets much worse, or a calf goes hot and swollen, or you get the headache or any spotting, don't wait for that Tuesday, come straight in.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): Hot calf, headache, spotting, come in. Can I still walk to the rank, or must I rest the leg?

[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Walking is good for you, keep it up, and stretch the calves before bed. Have the iron with orange juice if you can, not with tea or milk, leave the milk for an hour or two later.

[SEG0046] person_1 (PATIENT): Ok, we get the juice from the Spar. Umm, is a ferritin of 14 dangerous for the baby, because I read they come out small, and I even started measuring my belly with a tape, which I know is silly, and my boss asked if I need lighter duties.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): At 14, with you already on the iron, I'm not alarmed for the baby. No new tablet today. We'll keep an eye, and you're doing the right things.
[SEG0048] person_1 (PATIENT): Ok shame, thank you, that actually helps. I'll do the stretches, I'll try remember the Saturday tablet, and I'll see the midwife in two weeks.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Go well. Shout if anything changes before then.

spec.situation: Pregnant woman at 30 weeks with creeping legs at night and poor sleep; ferritin discussed; takes folic acid and iron; midwife check booked.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

bad.reason: Patient denies ankle swelling; doctor also sees no ankle puffiness.
bad.text: Ankle swelling (category=cardiovascular, status=present, frequency=by the evening, temporality=current, body_site=ankles, reported_by=clinical_staff, certainty=disputed)

omissions.text: Recorded symptom of ankle swelling is wrong: the patient explicitly denied ankle swelling, saying her ankles only feel heavy with no puffiness, shoes fit the same, and no sock marks.
Creeping sensation details not recorded: mainly from the right knee to the ankle, starts as soon as she lies down, and the left leg only sometimes joins in after standing too long.
Patient clarified sleep is not 'hardly at all': she does fall asleep around midnight and the problem is broken sleep with waking 4-5 times, not total insomnia.
Ferritin result value of 14 from last week is stated explicitly on the file.
Previous blood pressure at the last visit was 130/84 after repeat measurement.
Negative finding not recorded: no chest symptoms and specifically can walk and talk without gasping.
Negative finding not recorded: no burning/itching quality to the leg sensation; patient described it as 'not itchy, more like ants under the skin'.
Pregnancy/fetal wellbeing detail not recorded: baby is wriggling nicely, especially after cold water, more on the left.
Wound detail not recorded: shin cut from a bakkie door healed in five days, clean and dry with no oozing.
Family history detail not recorded: mother had neither diabetes nor hypertension and died in a car accident, not a stroke.
Plan detail not recorded: no new tablet was started today.
Follow-up detail not recorded: the two-week follow-up is the already-booked Tuesday morning antenatal/midwife clinic visit.
